title: Spreading a geometrically connected fibre open in a flat geometrically reduced family
statement: Let $h:Y\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Suppose that for every $t\in S$ the fibre $Y_t=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field] is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $s\in S$ and let $T\subseteq Y_s$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] geometrically connected over $\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; connected includes nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then there exist an affine scheme $S_1$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], an etale morphism $a:S_1\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $s_1\in S_1$ with $a(s_1)=s$ and $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s_1)$ an isomorphism, together with a quasi-compact open subscheme $V\subseteq Y\times_S S_1$, such that every fibre of $V\to S_1$ is geometrically connected and $V_{s_1}=T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_1)$ as open subschemes of $(Y\times_S S_1)_{s_1}$.

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $S_0\subseteq S$ of $s$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and replace $Y$ by $Y_0=Y\times_SS_0$. The morphism $h_0:Y_0\to S_0$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Its fibres over points of $S_0$ are the original fibres, since the open inclusion preserves the residue fields and the iterated fibre products agree [def-pc-base-change]. In particular $T$ is unchanged. An elementary etale neighbourhood constructed over $S_0$ is also one over $S$: the local affine charts and local ring maps defining etaleness [def-weil-etale-morphism] are unchanged by the open inclusion. In what follows rename $S_0,Y_0,h_0$ as $S,Y,h$.

source.place: Tag 055W, label lemma-fibre-geometrically-connected-reduced, first paragraph: affine localization of the base

proof.text: The fibre $Y_s$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $\kappa(s)$-algebras: use the finite-presentation charts of $h$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compactness of its fibre from clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], and the affine quasi-compactness of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] to select finitely many such charts. Each chart is a Noetherian topological space by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. Every open in such a space is quasi-compact: otherwise successively adjoining members of an open cover with no finite subcover yields a strictly increasing chain of open subsets, contradicting stabilization of their closed complements. The intersections of $T$ with the finitely many charts are therefore quasi-compact, so $T$ is quasi-compact. By the fibre homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre] there is an open $O\subseteq Y$ with $O_s=T$. Cover $T$ by affine opens of $Y$ contained in $O$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and take finitely many of them covering $T$. Their union $W\subseteq O$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and $W_s=T$ as open subschemes, because both have the induced open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 055W, label lemma-fibre-geometrically-connected-reduced, first paragraph: existence of the quasi-compact lift of the prescribed fibre open

proof.text: The open subscheme $W$ inherits flatness from $h$: the local ring map at each point is the same [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion]. For local finite presentation, refine the affine presentation charts by principal opens lying in $W$: if $B=A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$, then $B_b=B[u]/(bu-1)$ is still finitely presented over $A$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The affine base is quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $Y$ is quasi-separated by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Any two affine opens of $W$ are affine opens of $Y$ and have quasi-compact intersection by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion]. The converse clause makes $W$ quasi-separated. Since $W$ is quasi-compact, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $W\to S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence of finite presentation. Every field extension of a fibre of $W$ is an open in the corresponding field extension of a fibre of $Y$ [def-pc-base-change]; its local rings are the same reduced local rings [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Thus its fibres are geometrically reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Replace $Y$ by $W$, retaining that it is an open in the original family and that its whole designated fibre is $T$.

source.place: Tag 055W, label lemma-fibre-geometrically-connected-reduced, first paragraph: checking the restricted family hypotheses

proof.text: Let $C\subseteq Y$ be the fibrewise Cohen–Macaulay locus. It is open by [lem-sbc-fibre-cohen-macaulay-locus-open], and its intersection with $Y_s$ is dense by [lem-trf-flat-lfp-cm-locus-fibre-dense]. The fibre $Y_s=T$ is nonempty by geometric connectedness [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-connected-scheme], so $C\cap Y_s$ is a nonempty open of $Y_s$. This fibre is locally of finite type over $\kappa(s)$, as is immediate from its finitely presented affine charts. Apply [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] with the closed subset equal to all of $Y_s$: its closed points are dense, hence this nonempty open contains a point $y$ closed in $Y_s$. Its fibre local ring is Cohen–Macaulay. This verifies both the flatness and fibre-local-ring conditions at $y$, without asserting smoothness or separability of its residue field.

source.place: Tag 055W, label lemma-fibre-geometrically-connected-reduced, second paragraph: choice of the closed Cohen–Macaulay point

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cm-closed-point-flat-quasifinite-slice] at $y$. It gives $i:Z\to Y$ with $q=h\circ i$ flat and locally of finite presentation and with $Z_s$ a singleton $\{z\}$ mapping to $y$. In particular $q$ is locally of finite type (a finite presentation gives finite generators [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]) and $z$ is isolated in its fibre. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-finite-at-point-elementary] applies to $(q,z)$: obtain an etale $U\to S$, a point $u$ over $s$ with $\kappa(s)\simeq\kappa(u)$, and an open $E\subseteq Z\times_SU$ finite over $U$, with exactly one point over $u$. The latter assertion makes $E_u$ nonempty.

source.place: Tag 055W, label lemma-fibre-geometrically-connected-reduced, second paragraph: slicing and the elementary-etale finite piece

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood of $u$ in $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] and restrict $E$ to it. The restriction is still finite and still has exactly one point above $u$ by [lem-weil-pbc-elementary-etale-finite-piece-persistence], applied to the open inclusion, whose residue map at $u$ is the identity. Rename the affine neighbourhood $U$ and the restricted piece $E$. Etaleness of $U\to S$ is unchanged on these source-local charts [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The base change $Z_U\to U$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Its open restriction $E\to U$ has the same local ring maps and inherits the finite-presentation charts, so it is flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Together with finiteness this is precisely finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Restricting $i_U$ gives the required map $\sigma:E\to Y_U$ over $U$.

source.place: Tag 055W, label lemma-fibre-geometrically-connected-reduced, second paragraph: affine refinement and finite locally freeness

proof.text: The family $Y_U\to U$ is flat and of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). For $t\in U$ and every field extension $L/\kappa(t)$, its fibre extended to $L$ is $Y_{a(t)}\times_{\kappa(a(t))}L$, by the iterated-base-change identity [def-pc-base-change], and is reduced by the original geometric-reducedness hypothesis [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The whole fibre at $u$ is $Y_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(u)=T\times_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(u)$ and is geometrically connected: every extension of $\kappa(u)$ is also an extension of $\kappa(s)$, and the same iterated-base-change identity identifies its extension with that of $T$. We have also retained $E_u\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 055W, label lemma-fibre-geometrically-connected-reduced, second paragraph: hypotheses for connected-fibre descent

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-locally-free-multisection-connected-open] with $X=Y_U$, $B=U$, $Z=E$, the map $\sigma$ just constructed and the point $b_0=u$. Its finite-locally-free, nonempty designated fibre, flat finite-presentation, geometrically reduced, and geometrically connected designated fibre hypotheses were all checked in steps 6–7. It gives a quasi-compact open $V^0\subseteq Y_U$ with $V^0_u=(Y_U)_u$ as open subschemes and geometrically connected fibres wherever nonempty. Empty fibres away from $u$ are allowed at this stage.

source.place: Tag 055W, label lemma-fibre-geometrically-connected-reduced, second paragraph: application of connected-fibre descent

proof.text: The open restriction $V^0\to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by the unchanged local ring maps and restricted affine charts [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Hence its image $I\subseteq U$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. It contains $u$ since $V^0_u=T_{\kappa(u)}$ is nonempty. Choose an affine open $S_1\subseteq I$ containing $u$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], put $s_1=u$ and $V=V^0\times_US_1$. This remains quasi-compact: $V^0\to U$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), since $V^0$ is quasi-compact and $U$ is affine and thus quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; the inverse image of the quasi-compact affine open $S_1$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open]. Every fibre of $V\to S_1$ is nonempty, because $S_1\subseteq I$, and equals the corresponding fibre of $V^0\to U$, so is geometrically connected. Its designated fibre is exactly $T\times_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s_1)$ by [def-pc-base-change]. Since all source restrictions were opens, $V$ is an open subscheme of the original $Y\times_SS_1$. The map $S_1\to S$ remains etale on the same local charts [def-weil-etale-morphism], and its residue map at $s_1$ is the isomorphism already obtained. These are all the claimed properties.

source.place: Tag 055W, label lemma-fibre-geometrically-connected-reduced, final sentences: open image, affine shrinking, quasi-compactness and exact fibre equality
